label: prop:shell-structure-eigenvalues
title: Orbital shells from eigenvalues of the photon-electron transfer matrix
html:
Proposition (conditional on conj:borromean-quark — shell-structure eigenvalues from photon-electron transfer matrix). The eigenvalues of the photon-electron transfer matrix T_{\gamma e}(q) determine the orbital shell structure of an atom. Shell n corresponds to the n-th power T_{\gamma e}^n. The shell energies satisfy a Chebyshev recurrence in q.

The characteristic polynomial

The photon-electron transfer matrix (transfer matrix operator) is T_{\gamma e} = T_{pp}:

  T_{\gamma e}(q) = 
  \begin{pmatrix}
    q - q^{-1} & 1 \\
    1 & 0
  \end{pmatrix}

Its characteristic polynomial is:

  \det(T_{\gamma e} - \lambda \mathbb{I})
  = 
  \lambda^2 - (q - q^{-1})\lambda - 1
  =  0

This yields the eigenvalues:

  \lambda_{\pm}(q)
  = 
  \frac{(q - q^{-1}) \pm \sqrt{(q - q^{-1})^2 + 4}}{2}

The square root is spurious and the decimals below were wrong. Corrected 2026-08-09. The discriminant is a perfect square: (q-q^{-1})^2 + 4 = q^2 + 2 + q^{-2} = (q+q^{-1})^2, so \sqrt{h^2+4} = [2]_q exactly — the Temperley–Lieb loop parameter — and the eigenvalues are exact, with no radical and no decimal expansion:

  \lambda_\pm = \frac{h \pm [2]_q}{2}
  = \frac{(q-q^{-1}) \pm (q+q^{-1})}{2}
  \;\Longrightarrow\;
  \lambda_+ = q, \qquad \lambda_- = -q^{-1}.

These are of course the Hecke generator's eigenvalues — \lambda satisfies \lambda^2 = h\lambda + 1, i.e. (\lambda-q)(\lambda+q^{-1}) = 0 — which is what identifies this operator as \sigma_i rather than merely resembling it. See JonesNormalisation.tl_generator_sq.

The published numerics were also arithmetically wrong, independently of any convention: \sqrt{0.2091^2+4} = 2.01090, not 2.0054, and the eigenvalues follow the error.

published correct
\sqrt{h^2+4} 2.0054 2.010897 (= [2]_q)
\lambda_+ 1.1073 1.109979 (= q)
\lambda_- -0.9027 -0.900918 (= -q^{-1})

At the substrate parameter q (retained as published; see the correction above):

  q - q^{-1} = 0.2091, \quad
  \sqrt{0.2091^2 + 4} = 2.0054
  \lambda_+ = 1.1073, \quad
  \lambda_- = -0.9027

Shell n from the n-th power

Shell n of an atom is the n-th power of the transfer matrix at the electron-nucleus junction. Each power corresponds to one R-I move (Reidemeister I). This adds one curl to the electron trefoil, increasing the writhe by 1 without altering the knot type.

We diagonalize T_{\gamma e} = S \Lambda S^{-1}:

  T_{\gamma e}^n
  = 
  S
  \begin{pmatrix}
    \lambda_+^n & 0 \\
    0 & \lambda_-^n
  \end{pmatrix}
  S^{-1}

The eigenvector matrix is:

  S = 
  \begin{pmatrix}
    \lambda_+ & \lambda_- \\
    1 & 1
  \end{pmatrix}

The entries of T_{\gamma e}^n are:

  (T^n)_{11}
  = 
  \frac{\lambda_+^{n+1} - \lambda_-^{n+1}}{\lambda_+ - \lambda_-},
  \qquad
  (T^n)_{21}
  = 
  \frac{\lambda_+^n - \lambda_-^n}{\lambda_+ - \lambda_-}

These correspond to Chebyshev polynomials of the second kind in the variable \frac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1}):

  (T^n)_{21} =  U_{n-1}\!\left(\tfrac{q - q^{-1}}{2}\right)

The traced volume at shell n

The Markov-traced volume at shell n is:

  \hat{V}(n, q)
  = 
  z \cdot (T^n)_{11} + (T^n)_{21}
  = 
  \frac{(z\lambda_+ + 1)\lambda_+^n - (z\lambda_- + 1)\lambda_-^n}
       {\lambda_+ - \lambda_-}

where z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1) is the Markov parameter (convention D).

We define:

  \alpha =  z\lambda_+ + 1, \qquad
  \beta =  z\lambda_- + 1

This gives:

  \hat{V}(n, q) = 
  \frac{\alpha \cdot \lambda_+^n - \beta \cdot \lambda_-^n}
       {\lambda_+ - \lambda_-}

Since |\lambda_+| > 1 > |\lambda_-|, the dominant term for large n becomes:

  \hat{V}(n, q)  \sim 
  \frac{\alpha}{\lambda_+ - \lambda_-} \cdot \lambda_+^n
  \qquad (n \gg 1)

The sub-dominant term \beta \cdot \lambda_-^n = \beta \cdot (-1)^n / \lambda_+^n provides an alternating correction that decays exponentially.

The Chebyshev recurrence

The traced volumes satisfy the three-term recurrence:

  \boxed{
    \hat{V}(n+1, q)
    = 
    (q - q^{-1}) \cdot \hat{V}(n, q)
    + 
    \hat{V}(n-1, q)
  }

The initial conditions are \hat{V}(0, q) = 1 (no crossings) and \hat{V}(1, q) = z(q - q^{-1}) + 1 (one crossing).
